reasoning: The claim is scientifically accurate. Reliable scientific and educational sources, including the Smithsonian Institution, the Natural History Museum, and New Scientist, confirm that octopuses possess three hearts and blue blood. Two of their hearts (the branchial hearts) pump blood through the gills to collect oxygen, while the third, central heart (the systemic heart) circulates this oxygenated blood to the rest of the body. Their blood is blue due to the presence of a copper-rich protein called hemocyanin (instead of the iron-based hemoglobin found in humans), which turns blue when oxygenated and becomes clear or colorless when deoxygenated.
